proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(g_i^{ab}=\Gamma_i[a,b]\) for \(i\in\{1,2\}\) and \(a,b\in M\).  We first verify that the displayed construction is in the maintained model class.  By \(\text{def:strictness-example}\), the two stacked vectors \((\varepsilon_1^{(a)})_{a\in M}\) and \((\varepsilon_2^{(a)})_{a\in M}\) are independent centered Gaussian vectors.  Their concatenation is therefore centered Gaussian, and \(X\), being a linear transformation of that concatenation under the displayed structural equations, is jointly centered Gaussian.  Thus \(\text{ass:centered-gaussian-law}\) holds.  Independence of the two stacks implies, for every \(a,b\in M\),
\[
\operatorname{Cov}_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}(\varepsilon_1^{(a)},\varepsilon_2^{(b)})=0,
\]
which is \(\text{ass:cross-variable-disturbance-orthogonality}\) when \(V=\{1,2\}\).

It remains to verify disturbance nondegeneracy.  The matrix \(\Gamma_1\) has the equicorrelation form with diagonal \(1\) and off-diagonal entry \(1/5\), so its eigenvalues are
\[
1-\frac15=\frac45\quad\text{with multiplicity two},
\qquad
1+2\frac15=\frac75.
\]
Hence \(\Gamma_1\succ0\).  The leading principal minors of \(\Gamma_2\) are
\[
1,
\qquad
1-\frac1{25}=\frac{24}{25},
\qquad
\det(\Gamma_2)
=1+2\frac15\frac25\frac15-\frac1{25}-\frac4{25}-\frac1{25}
=\frac{99}{125}.
\]
All three are positive, so Sylvester's criterion gives \(\Gamma_2\succ0\).  Thus \(\text{ass:disturbance-nondegeneracy}\) holds.  Finally, the equations in \(\text{def:strictness-example}\) can be written
\[
X^{(a)}=
\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix}X^{(a)}+\varepsilon^{(a)},
\qquad a\in M,
\]
so \(\text{ass:linear-structural-equations}\) holds, and the displayed matrix is strictly lower triangular in the order \((1,2)\), which verifies \(\text{ass:shared-topological-order}\).  Every member property in \(\text{def:component-aligned-limvam-class}\) has now been checked, proving
\[
(P_{\mathrm{ex}},B^0,\varepsilon,\Gamma,(1,2))\in\mathfrak M_{2,3}^{\mathrm{CA}}.
\]

We next calculate the observed moment restrictions.  From
\(X_1^{(a)}=\varepsilon_1^{(a)}\) and
\(X_2^{(a)}=\varepsilon_1^{(a)}+\varepsilon_2^{(a)}\), cross-variable disturbance orthogonality gives, for every \(a,b\in M\),
\[
\Sigma^{ab}
=\begin{pmatrix}
g_1^{ab}&g_1^{ab}\\
g_1^{ab}&g_1^{ab}+g_2^{ab}
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Both displayed disturbance covariance matrices have unit diagonal.  Consequently, for every \(a\in M\),
\[
\Sigma^{aa}=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \det(\Sigma^{aa})=1>0.
\]
In particular, every inverse required by \(\text{def:modified-cholesky}\) exists.

For the order \((1,2)\), the only nonzero order-constrained regression coefficient is
\[
B_{(1,2)}^{(a)}[2,1]
=\Sigma^{aa}[2,1]\{\Sigma^{aa}[1,1]\}^{-1}=1,
\]
and hence, in every view,
\[
B_{(1,2)}^{(a)}=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
L_{(1,2)}^{(a)}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Using \(\text{def:residual-cross-blocks}\), direct multiplication yields
\[
R_{(1,2)}^{ab}
=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}g_1^{ab}&g_1^{ab}\\g_1^{ab}&g_1^{ab}+g_2^{ab}\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}g_1^{ab}&0\\0&g_2^{ab}\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Thus the true order satisfies the diagonal residual restriction for every pair of views.

For the reverse order \((2,1)\), the only nonzero coefficient is the regression coefficient of \(X_1^{(a)}\) on its predecessor \(X_2^{(a)}\):
\[
B_{(2,1)}^{(a)}[1,2]
=\Sigma^{aa}[1,2]\{\Sigma^{aa}[2,2]\}^{-1}=\frac12.
\]
Therefore, again in every view,
\[
B_{(2,1)}^{(a)}=\begin{pmatrix}0&1/2\\0&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
L_{(2,1)}^{(a)}=\begin{pmatrix}1&-1/2\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
A second multiplication gives the complete reverse-order residual block
\[
R_{(2,1)}^{ab}
=\begin{pmatrix}
\dfrac{g_1^{ab}+g_2^{ab}}4&\dfrac{g_1^{ab}-g_2^{ab}}2\\[4pt]
\dfrac{g_1^{ab}-g_2^{ab}}2&g_1^{ab}+g_2^{ab}
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
It follows that the reverse order is compatible with a view pair \(\{a,b\}\) if and only if
\[
g_1^{ab}=g_2^{ab}.
\]

Take \(H=\{1,2\}\).  The construction gives
\(g_1^{12}=g_2^{12}=1/5\), so the residual cross-block of each of the two orders is diagonal on the only distinct calibrated pair.  By \(\text{def:compatible-orders}\), and because \(\mathfrak S_{\{1,2\}}\) contains exactly these two permutations,
\[
\Pi_H(\mathcal O_H)=\{(1,2),(2,1)\}.
\]
The coefficient calculations above and \(\text{def:identified-tuple-set}\) therefore imply
\[
\Theta_H(\mathcal O_H)
=\left\{
\left(\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\right)_{a\in M},
\left(\begin{pmatrix}0&1/2\\0&0\end{pmatrix}\right)_{a\in M}
\right\}.
\]
These two tuples are numerically distinct, since their \((2,1)\) and \((1,2)\) entries differ.  By \(\text{lem:fixed-order-residual-characterization}\), these compatibility calculations are not merely formal regression tests: each order supplies a full positive-definite component-aligned Gaussian completion of \(\mathcal O_H\), and the displayed set is the complete coefficient equivalence class.

Under full calibration, the pair \(\{1,3\}\) is observed.  Here
\[
g_1^{13}=\frac15,
\qquad
g_2^{13}=\frac25,
\qquad
R_{(2,1)}^{13}[1,2]
=R_{(2,1)}^{13}[2,1]
=-\frac1{10}\ne0.
\]
Thus the reverse order is not in \(\Pi_M(\mathcal O_M)\).  The true order is in that set because all of its residual cross-blocks are diagonal, and there are no other permutations.  Hence
\[
\Pi_M(\mathcal O_M)=\{(1,2)\},
\qquad
\Theta_M(\mathcal O_M)
=\left\{\left(\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\right)_{a\in M}\right\},
\]
where the second equality follows from \(\text{def:identified-tuple-set}\).

Finally, the displayed coefficient and disturbance parameter belongs to
\(\Omega_{(1,2)}^{\mathrm{CA}}\) by the already verified strict lower-triangularity and positive definiteness.  For the calibrated pair \(\{1,2\}\), both off-diagonal reverse-order residual entries vanish.  The principal-minor denominators used in \(\text{def:pairwise-exceptional-variety}\) are positive because every \(\Sigma^{aa}\succ0\); therefore denominator clearing preserves whether each entry is zero.  Hence
\[
f_{(2,1),12}^{12}(\theta)=f_{(2,1),21}^{12}(\theta)=0,
\qquad
F_{(2,1)}^{12}(\theta)=0.
\]
Since \((2,1)\) is the only permutation different from \((1,2)\), the defining product for \(\mathcal E_{12,(1,2)}\) vanishes, and so \(\theta\in\mathcal E_{12,(1,2)}\).  In contrast, the calculation \(R_{(2,1)}^{13}[1,2]=-1/10\) shows that the reverse-order restriction fails on the fully observed pair \(\{1,3\}\), exactly because \(\Gamma_1[1,3]=1/5\ne2/5=\Gamma_2[1,3]\).  This proves every assertion.

Put \(S=\{a,b\}\).  Because \(\theta\in\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\setminus\mathcal E_{ab,\pi_0}\), the fixed-pair conclusion of \(\text{thm:generic-calibration-elbow}\) gives
\[
\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)=\{\pi_0\}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)=\{T_{\pi_0}\}.
\tag{1}
\]
This is an equality between the structural equivalence class and the observable recovery map, rather than a definition of the structural target: it follows from the exceptional-variety argument and the residual characterization contained in that theorem.

We next verify the asserted positivity of the feasibility margin.  For each \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\setminus\{\pi_0\}\), define the proof-intermediate number
\[
c_\pi
:=
\max_{\{u,v\}\in\binom S2}
\bigl\|\operatorname{offdiag}(R_\pi^{uv})\bigr\|_{\max}.
\tag{2}
\]
By (1), such a \(\pi\) is not in \(\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)\).  The defining equivalence in \(\text{def:compatible-orders}\) therefore implies that at least one observed pair has a nonzero off-diagonal residual entry, and hence
\[
c_\pi>0.
\tag{3}
\]
There are exactly \(p!-1\) such permutations; this collection is finite and nonempty because \(p\ge2\).  Using (1)--(3) in \(\text{def:feasibility-margin}\) yields
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{feas}}(\mathcal O_S)
=
\min_{\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\setminus\{\pi_0\}}c_\pi
>0,
\tag{4}
\]
since the minimum of a finite nonempty family of strictly positive real numbers is strictly positive.

Now impose \(\text{ass:calibration-sampling}\) and \(\text{ass:marginal-sampling}\), so the aligned observations from \(S\) and every viewwise marginal are sampled from the same law \(P\).  Impose also \(\text{ass:feasibility-separation}\) and \(\text{ass:path-product-separation}\), which respectively give
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{feas}}(\mathcal O_S)\ge\kappa_{\mathrm{feas}}>0,
\qquad
\delta_{\mathrm{path}}(\mathcal O_S)\ge\kappa_{\mathrm{path}}>0.
\tag{5}
\]
The parameter-space condition \(\theta\in\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\) induces a centered component-aligned Gaussian law and imposes \(\Gamma_i\succ0\) for every \(i\in V\).  In particular, every scalar \(\Gamma_i[a,a]\) and every principal block \(\Gamma_i[S,S]\) is positive definite.  Because each \(I_p-B^{(a)}\) is unit triangular in the order \(\pi_0\), it is invertible, and the covariance formula in that parameter-space definition gives
\[
\Sigma^{aa}
=(I_p-B^{(a)})^{-1}
\operatorname{diag}_{i\in V}\!\bigl(\Gamma_i[a,a]\bigr)
(I_p-B^{(a)})^{-\mathsf T}
\succ0.
\tag{6}
\]
Likewise, after grouping the selected disturbances by variable label, their covariance is \(\bigoplus_{i\in V}\Gamma_i[S,S]\succ0\); the block-diagonal structural transformation with blocks \((I_p-B^{(a)})^{-1}\), \(a\in S\), is invertible, so \(\Sigma^{SS}\succ0\).  Hence all Gaussian and covariance-positivity conditions of \(\text{thm:covariance-region-inversion}\) hold, and all inverses used by its modified-Cholesky maps are well defined.  Together with the four assumptions just cited, that theorem applies whenever its displayed finite-sample conditions \(\eta_{S,n}<1\) and \(\eta_{a,n}<1\) hold.

Let the sourcewise sample sizes tend to infinity, let \(\alpha_n\to0\), and suppose the radii in \(\text{def:covariance-region}\) vanish as stated in the proposition.  The consistency conclusion of \(\text{thm:covariance-region-inversion}\), applied using (5), gives
\[
d_{\mathrm H}^{d_{\mathrm{coef}}}
\!\left(
\widehat\Theta_{S,n}(\alpha_n),
\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)
\right)
\xrightarrow{P}0
\tag{7}
\]
and
\[
\Pr\!\left\{
\widehat\prec_{S,n}(\alpha_n)=\prec_S
\right\}
\longrightarrow1.
\tag{8}
\]
Substitution of (1) into (7) proves Hausdorff recovery of the singleton \(\{T_{\pi_0}\}\).  Finally, by \(\text{def:essential-poset}\) and the singleton equality in (1), \(i\prec_S j\) holds exactly when the union support graph \(G_{T_{\pi_0}}\) contains a directed path from \(i\) to \(j\).  Hence \(\prec_S\) is the ancestral relation induced by \(T_{\pi_0}\), and (8) is exact recovery of that induced ancestral poset.
